Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed BrightPath's redline and pulled precedent from our last few MSA negotiations with marketplace customers. High-level guidance: we should not accept a broad, one-way exception that treats lost margin as recoverable in every circumstance. That would materially increase our exposure and create asymmetric risk.

Two recommended paths (with suggested clause language):

Option 1 (Preferred): Mutual exclusion with a very narrow reliance carve-out-
"Except for liability arising from (i) the parties' payment obligations under this Agreement, (ii) gross negligence or willful misconduct, and (iii) any claims by a third party to the extent such claims are attributable to a Party's breach of confidentiality or IP obligations, neither Party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, indirect or punitive damages, including lost profits, lost margin, loss of business, or loss of data. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may recover direct reliance damages in an amount not to exceed the aggregate fees paid or payable to Redwood under the Order Form for the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim."

Rationale: this preserves a mutual exclusion (commercially acceptable), carves out payment obligations and severe wrongdoing, and allows a capped, measurable reliance remedy (aggregate fees is an easy cap).

Option 2: Clarify definitions and keep exclusion absolute-
"'Consequential Losses' means losses that are not the direct result of the breach and include, without limitation, lost profits, lost margin, loss of business, loss of reputation, and punitive or exemplary damages. The Parties expressly agree that consequential losses are excluded from recoverable damages under this Agreement, except for third-party claims to the extent set forth in Section X.'"

Rationale: gives us a bright-line definition that procurement may find harder to accept, but it limits interpretation disputes.

Next steps: if sales wants to present Option 1 to BrightPath, I can prepare a tracked redline with the exact language and a short procurement memo explaining the cap and why it's acceptable from a risk perspective. If we go Option 2, I recommend a short call between legal and BrightPath counsel to walk the definition through examples.

I've uploaded a sample redline to DocuSign for ease of signature once both sides agree to the wording.
